title: COMMON DISEASES IN DAIRY CATTLE
text:
COMMON DISEASES IN DAIRY CATTLE

Objectives:
1. To be able to identify the healthy from sick animals.
2. To know the common diseases in calves.
3. To know the common diseases in heifers and cows.
4. To be able to know how to manage and prevent the common diseases in dairy cattle.

Healthy vs. Sick

| | HEALTHY | SICK |
|---|---|---|
| Eyes | Bright, alert | Dull, depress, dehydrated, lacrimate |
| Nose | Moist and clean | Dry, nasal discharges |
| Ears | Erect, alert | Droop |
| Skin and coat | Shiny, smooth | Dry, dehydrated |
| Social behavior | With the herd | Isolated from the herd |
| Activity | Normal | Recumbent, inappetent |
| Production | Normal | Sudden decrease |

10 Health check protocol:

1. TEMPERATURE – normal temperature of adult dairy cattle is 38.5-39.0°C.

facts: The learning objectives include identifying healthy from sick animals, knowing common diseases in calves, heifers, and cows, and learning how to manage and prevent them.
Healthy cattle have bright and alert eyes, whereas sick cattle have dull, depressed, dehydrated, or lacrimating eyes.
Healthy cattle have a moist and clean nose, while sick cattle have a dry nose or nasal discharges.
Healthy cattle have erect and alert ears, whereas sick cattle have drooping ears.
The skin and coat of healthy cattle are shiny and smooth, whereas sick cattle have dry and dehydrated skin and coat.
In terms of social behavior, healthy cattle stay with the herd, while sick cattle become isolated from the herd.
Healthy cattle display normal activity, whereas sick cattle may be recumbent and inappetent.
Milk production remains normal in healthy cattle, but sick cattle show a sudden decrease in production.
The normal body temperature of adult dairy cattle is 38.5°C to 39.0°C.
A rectal thermometer is used to measure the body temperature of a cow.
Body temperature in dairy cattle can increase due to weather conditions, the estrus cycle, or the presence of an infection.
The second item listed under the 10 Health check protocol is 'DUNG OR MANURE'.
